messages:
maria: :rotating_light: Seeing a spike in warmup queue depth and tail latencies for hosted inference, paging oncall. Customers hitting 504s. 

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-8474. Severity: P2. Paging oncall. Log group: /redwood/inference/production.

kai: I can grab this. Starting from current metrics — queue_length jumped to ~220 for the small-gpu pool at 02:46 UTC, HPA reported scaling events but pods stayed terminating for ~30s each.

anjali: Confirmed: request_latency_p99 for generate endpoint hit 6.8s, error rate up to 8% (mostly 504s). Most failures are warmup timeouts.

devon: Stack trace from logs: ```[2024-12-28T02:46:15Z] pool=small-gpu id=gp-13 warmup_start model=rwkv-14B quant=8bit
[2024-12-28T02:46:45Z] pool=small-gpu id=gp-13 warmup_error timeout after 30s
[2024-12-28T02:47:01Z] router queue_depth=215 route=/v1/generate fallback=false
```

maria: Hypothesis: autoscaler HPA triggers too late because memory-based metric underestimates required headroom for warmup; pods are created but warmup stalls due to intense concurrent arrivals causing KV-cache misses and long load times.

kai: Repro note: burst of small requests with long context/seq len spike load on warmup. HPA uses cpu% and pod memory but warmup relies on GPU allocation and model weights loading.

anjali: Quick mitigation options: 1) enable reserved burst pool (if available) 2) route new requests to fallback smaller model 3) temporarily lower HPA threshold to scale earlier 4) increase warmup concurrency limit. Thoughts?

devon: I can flip routing to fallback smaller model (rwkv-7B) for non-SLA customers to reduce load. Doing canary route now. 

kai: +1, do that. Also enabling autoscale warmup config: setting min_replicas=4 for small-gpu pool to provide headroom. Executing kubectl patch now.

maria: I will notify support & product for customer impact. Which customers are affected?

anjali: Support shows ~12 orgs with elevated error rates, top affected are "docscribe" and "chatforms". Notifying CSMs now.

incidence-bot: (system) Deploybot: rolled canary route for fallback model to 12% of traffic.

tim: Patch command used: ```kubectl -n inference patch hpa small-gpu-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4,"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":40}}'``` Applied. Confirming kube API accepted.

kai: After min_replicas bump and route switch, queue_depth dropped from 215 -> 48 in ~90s, error rate down to 1.3%. Warmup latencies still elevated but improving.

maria: Good. We should collect logs for RCA: pod lifecycle events, HPA events, router trace, and kernel warmup timings. Please capture 02:30-03:10 UTC window.

devon: Pulling logs now. Key snippets saved to /shared/incidents/INC-2024-8474/logs.txt. Extracted events: 02:44 HPA scale event triggered, 02:44:05 pods scheduled, 02:44:25 pods starting warmup, 02:44:55 warmup timeouts.

anjali: Adding timeline entry: 
- 02:42: request surge begins (series of long-context requests)
- 02:44: HPA observes CPU spike, attempts to scale
- 02:44-02:46: new pods scheduled, but warmup blocked by simultaneous weight loads -> long I/O on NFS cache tier
- 02:46: router qlen peaks 220 -> backpressure observed
- 02:47: retries and timeouts increase, customer 504s
- 02:49: mitigation: fallback routing + min_replica bump -> recovery by 02:51

maria: Hypotheses to track in RCA: 
- H1: HPA signal too coarse and slow for warmup-heavy surges (metric mismatch)
- H2: Model weight loading contends on shared storage (NFS) causing warmup stalls when many pods start concurrently
- H3: Router scheduling allows cold-start request placement onto pods that are still warming -> no backoff to fallback variants early enough

kai: I ran a quick ddtrace: NFS read latency peaked at 430ms per file during the spike. That supports H2.

devon: Also saw high nvme egress on nodes hosting pools; maybe cache eviction thrash. Will get node-level iostat.

anjali: Action items right now: 
- kai: collect full HPA event timeline + metrics (cpu/mem/gpu_alloc) (ETA 10m)
- devon: node iostat, nvme metrics, and kernel logs (ETA 15m)
- maria: customer impact note + CSM sync (in progress)
- tim: evaluate router policy to prevent cold-start placement (postmortem work)

maria: I'll hand off to @sre-oncall for overnight watch and follow ups. SRE, take ownership for continuing RCA and mitigation tasks.

sre-oncall: Taking it. Leaving a follow-up runbook to validate: 1) implement staggered warmup on pod boot 2) prefetch model weights to local NVMe 3) adjust HPA to include queue_depth metric or custom warmup metric.

kai: One more note: observed warmup failure pattern: pods that start after 20 concurrent warmups fail more often. Need to add warmup concurrency guard.

devon: Uploaded logs + metrics to incident folder and linked in PagerDuty incident. https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-2024-8474/logs 

maria: Thanks team. I'll close the live mitigation call once SRE confirms monitoring thresholds and fallbacks are in place. Leaving this thread for RCA coordination. :thumbsup:
